truths.truth: A config key names the per-role dispatch-window ceiling and a `planning.mjs trace` surface reports a per-role crossing of it in the `budget-overrun` shape, read off the `tokens` on `brackets[]` rows
truths.evidence: Six `workflow.max_dispatch_tokens.<role>` int keys at cadence-core/config.schema.json:32-37 (planner/executor 200000, assumptions-analyzer/reviewer 150000, verifier 100000, plan-checker 75000). Value traced end to end: cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs:3265-3305 resolves DISPATCH_WINDOW_DEFAULTS through mergeLayers, feeds `windowBudget(r.file, r.brackets, ceilings)` (cadence-core/bin/lib/window-budget.mjs), and emits the problems. Live probe `node cadence-core/bin/planning.mjs trace window --phase 4` returned ceilings + 4 problems, each `{kind:"budget-overrun", file:".planning/trace.jsonl", detail:"cad-executor (corr 4-0e7e70e, phase 4, plan 1, return at ...): 245828 exceeds budget 200000 by 45828"}` - role named, compared 18, unbudgeted {"(no role)":1}, unrecorded 2. `trace window` also carries its CONTRACTS row at cadence-core/bin/self-verify.mjs:382 (`'trace window': ['--phase']`).

truths.truth: The ceiling's value is argued in shipped prose from named trace.jsonl keys with the per-role figures, and no dispatch is refused - the crossing is a post-hoc finding
truths.evidence: cadence-core/references/seams.md:67-95 states the ceiling is 'READ, never applied', names the budgeted quantity as the `tokens` on a `brackets[]` row of `.planning/trace.jsonl` read as a FINAL-WINDOW PROXY, and lists every default with its derivation (p75 rounded up to the next 25,000: cad-executor n=72 p75 182,631 max 275,285; cad-planner n=28 p75 188,135; cad-verifier n=24 p75 82,633; cad-reviewer n=2 p75 125,100; cad-plan-checker n=5 p75 64,203; cad-assumptions-analyzer n=25 p75 145,054). Non-refusal verified by reach: `grep -rn max_dispatch_tokens cadence-core agents skills` finds it only in the schema, planning.mjs:3282 (the report), self-verify comments, tests, report.md:43 and the six config-reach.md:125-130 rows, all reading 'trace window report only' - no agent frontmatter, dispatch path or spawn seam consults it. The live `trace window` run returned ok:true with 4 crossings and nothing refused.

truths.truth: The bulk-output rule is stated exactly once, in references/conventions.md, with a frozen register in cadence-core/bin/lib/ that carries no copy of the words
truths.evidence: `grep -rn 'rides a file, not the transcript' cadence-core agents skills` returns exactly one hit: cadence-core/references/conventions.md:97 (the rule runs :93-112 - measured threshold from .planning/reads.jsonl, the `> "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<name>"` transport, the digest requirement, the no-new-seam clause, and the pointer at the register). No copy in cadence-core/bin/lib/bulk-output.mjs (17 register rows at :191-298, exports BULK_OUTPUT/BULK_SHAPES/CODES/bulkOutputIssues). The two test files that grep as containing 'rides a file' assemble the clause from halves on purpose (prose-agreement.test.mjs:1285 `['rides a file','not the transcript'].join(', ')`), so the single-carrier assertion is not reporting on itself.

truths.truth: self-verify bites when a registered bulk-output site regresses to riding the transcript, and reports an unclassified site rather than skipping it
truths.evidence: Behavior observed without mutating any file, by calling the pure rule on modified text: bulkOutputIssues('cadence-core/references/triage-gate.md', <shipped text>) returns [] ; with the redirect stripped it returns [{kind:'bulk-output-inline', file:'cadence-core/references/triage-gate.md', detail:'`trace render --phase <N>` is registered as riding a scratch file and this line prescribes it with the output in the transcript...'}]; an unregistered `trace render --phase 9` call in a novel surface returns [{kind:'bulk-output-unregistered', ...'is classified by no row in lib/bulk-output.mjs - register it ... or out of scope with the reason'}]. Wired: cadence-core/bin/self-verify.mjs:184 imports it and :868 pushes its issues for every prose surface in the walk; the envelope's ok is `problems.length === 0` (:1460), so a bite exits non-zero. Full-tree run today: ok:true, problems [].
